POST /artifacts/{id}/reviews pins the latest version and every live write re-arms the settle timer: the new api tests use a 2 s window and assert the review's Version and the version's markdown, so a lost race fails as setup rather than passing on a row-true A; three consecutive head runs and the base run all held the window.

The spec's `selected` case is not reachable over HTTP (the edits route and uploads discard server-owned ask attributes for the row's); the Go test writes it through the server's own live attribute path (setLiveBlockAttributes) as the sibling does, and the live HTTP drive takes the decided-wording branch of the same predicate (an agent's reword of a decided block through the edits route). Describe no document-socket forgery as a procedure anywhere.
deviations: Plan 3.2 said TestAnApprovedVersionHoldingARepeatedBlockIDCarriesNothing would be red on the base (askBlockStates keeping the first node and carrying). It is green on the base: storedVersionTree reads A through pmdoc.ParseRendering, whose EnsureBlockIDs repairs a repeated id by minting a fresh one for the second block, so A shows a block N never had and carryVerdict's still-stands test refused on the base too (verified by the base run, /tmp/l752/red-on-base-docs.log, and by reading pmdoc/parse.go parseStampedAt and pmdoc/block_ids.go EnsureBlockIDsCount). The test is kept as a behavioural pin (green before and after); readApprovedVersion still reads A through askNodes as the plan asks, and its doc comment, the file comment, the learning and the changelog state that the refusal is unreachable from a stored version and what refuses a stored repeat instead. Two of the plan's three new tests are red on the base, not three.
openQuestions: For the architect: the plan's section 9 names the repeated-id refusal on A as a decision inside the spec's rule; it turns out to be a no-op for stored versions (the parser repairs the repeat first). Keeping the askNodes read in readApprovedVersion costs one branch and keeps A read exactly as N is; dropping it would discard askNodes' second return. I kept it with an honest comment. If you prefer it gone, say so in the review round.
For the architect: #1944's PR body still carries the Fast-follow line naming this residual; striking it there is yours.
discoveredComplexity: pmdoc.ParseRendering (parseStampedAt) runs EnsureBlockIDs on every stored version read back, so no reader of a stored version ever sees a repeated block id: the second block gets a minted id. Any rule that wants to treat a stored repeat specially must look at the markdown before the parse, or count BlockIDRepairCount; the carry needs neither, since the minted id already fails the still-stands test.
